title: Sector-memory obstruction to probe-level bath emergence in finite programmable qubit environments
summary: Finite quantum environments can relax local probes without acting as canonical baths. We study this distinction for a probe qubit coupled to a programmable bath of ($N$) qubits under excitation-number-conserving dynamics. The conserved charge partitions the Hilbert space into sectors. We characterize probe-level bath emergence using the sector-resolved late-time population ($p_e^{(q)}$), the sector-memory variance ($M_N$), and a global Gibbs-fit error ($Δ_G^{\mathrm{global}}$).
